title: The first minute
hookLine: what you do in your first waking minute shapes the day
tomorrow: a full moon, a hall of monks, and the Buddha teaches… breathing?

lines: THE PHONE HANDS YOU THE DAY.
A WHOLE CITY AT ONE DOOR.
cards: The alarm goes off, and before your feet find the floor, the phone has already handed you the day: a group chat, the news, somebody's vacation. Mark's Gospel tells about a morning that went another way.
The evening before, in the town of Capernaum, the whole city gathered at one door, bringing the sick to Jesus as the sun went down. Late that night the house finally goes quiet.
And in the dark, the man everyone wants is gone.

teach.h: RISING UP A GREAT WHILE BEFORE DAY.
teach.b: Mark says it in one line: "And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed." Simon and the others go looking.
When they find him, their first words land like a buzzing phone: "All men seek for thee." Everyone's waiting. Come back.
He says, let us go on to the next towns, because that is what I came out for. The hour alone came first, and out of it came his answer to the crowd. Here is the teaching under the story.
In Mark, Jesus slips away alone to pray at turning points: here, again after he feeds the crowd, and in Gethsemane.

teach.h: THE FIRST OF THE DAY, GIVEN FIRST.
teach.b: Some Christians have taken that solitary place as a pattern for an ordinary day: the first of the day is given to God before anyone else can claim it.
They call it a morning watch or a quiet time, a few minutes of prayer or scripture before the coffee and the crowd. Notice what the prayer did and didn't do. The crowd didn't vanish.
He met them knowing what he was for.
On your own path you can borrow this with the tag left on: Mark's morning, a first minute given away on purpose, before the day starts giving orders.

how: Some Christians keep a morning watch or quiet time, a few minutes of prayer or scripture before the day begins, following Gospel pictures like Mark's of Jesus praying alone before dawn.

o: the start of the day, given on purpose before it's claimed
the hardest minute of the morning, getting out of bed
a minute of silence held for someone who has died

where he went instead of back

s: once the disciples found him, Jesus went back to the waiting crowd
he said let us go on to the next towns. the prayer came first, then his answer.
the prayer before dawn came after a crowded evening at the door
the whole city gathered at the door at sunset; he rose a great while before day.
a morning quiet time is a rule every church requires

games.q: your sister's first move every morning is checking who needs her. by Mark's picture of Jesus' morning, what goes first?
o: a short time alone, given on purpose, and then the people who need her.
everyone's messages first, so the quiet later is guilt-free.
no people at all that day; the solitary place is the whole point.
games.why: Mark's Jesus didn't hide from the crowd. he prayed first, then went out to the towns knowing what he was for.

practice: Open yesterday's notebook and write tomorrow's first minute by hand: where your feet land, what your hands do, what you'll say or think before the phone.
If you pray, that minute might hold a line of prayer, the way Jesus kept the dark hour; if not, it might hold a window, a breath, a glass of water. Keep it to one minute you could really keep.

wordCard.voice: The first minute: the opening of the day, given on purpose before anything else claims it. In Mark, a solitary place, a great while before day.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: the first minute, and in Mark the prayer came before the crowd. The daily practice has begun.
